trial_court: Court of Principal Judge, Family Court, Muzaffarpur, Bihar (Matrimonial Case No. 82/2023)
case_name: Doly Rani vs Manish Kumar Chanchal
facts_of_case: Petitioner and respondent are trained commercial pilots who got married on 07.07.2021. They obtained a marriage certificate from Vadik Jankalyan Samiti (Regd.). The parties lived separately but differences ignited between them. Petitioner filed an FIR against the respondent's family members alleging harassment.

legal_principles.principle: A Hindu marriage must be performed with the requisite ceremonies in accordance with applicable customs or usage.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, requisite ceremonies for the solemnisation of the Hindu marriage must be in accordance with the applicable customs or usage and where saptapadi has been adopted, the marriage becomes complete and binding when the seventh step is taken.

legal_principles.principle: A mere issuance of a certificate by an entity in the absence of the requisite ceremonies having been performed does not confirm any marital status to the parties nor establish a marriage under Hindu law.
legal_principles.held: Unless the parties have undergone such ceremony, there would be no Hindu marriage according to Section 7 of the Act and a mere issuance of a certificate by an entity in the absence of the requisite ceremonies having been performed, would neither confirm any marital status to the parties nor establish a marriage under Hindu law.

outcome.final_order: The present transfer petition is allowed and the divorce petition under Section 13(1)(ia) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 bearing Matrimonial Case No. 82/2023 titled 'Manish Kumar v/s Doly Singh' pending before the Court of Principal Judge, Family Court, Muzaffarpur, Bihar is transferred to the Court of Principal Judge, Family Court, Ranchi Jharkhand.
